messages:
maya: Quick sync — finalizing the telemetry contract for the new runtime dashboards. We need sign-off on metric names, label schema (to avoid cardinality issues), alert thresholds (SLO burn mapping), and pager routing. Who's got time to review now?
ryan: I can take a pass. Can you paste the exact metric names and a few example queries so I can validate panels and alert rules?
maya: Sure — current proposal (prod-focused):
- runtime.request_latency_p50, runtime.request_latency_p95 (labels: env, region, model_family, customer_tier, shard)
- kv_cache.hit_rate (env, region, host_pool)
- model.queue_depth (env, model_family, shard)
- model.inflight_tokens (env, model_family)
- runtime.errors_5xx (env, region, model_family)
- deployment.gpu_utilization (env, host_pool)
- slo.burn_rate_estimate (calculated)
Example PromQL for p95 panel: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_family))`
And SLO burn estimate (rough): `sum(rate(error_budget_consumed[1m])) / sum(error_budget_total)` — need ops to confirm exact calc.
jess: FYI we should avoid putting raw `model_id` as a label on high-cardinality counters. Use `model_family` + sampled `model_id` tag (1% signals) if we need lookup in traces. Host pools and shard are ok.
ryan: +1 on sampled model_id. Also ask: do we want per-customer tiers on all panels or just on the SLO/alerting ones? Per-customer will blow up series.
maya: Keep per-customer in SLO/alerting rollups only (aggregate by customer_tier). Panels will default to model_family/regional slices.
anika: For alerting thresholds: propose two-tier burn alerts:
- Warning: slo.burn_rate_estimate > 1.2 for 10m (route to runtime-oncall)
- Critical: slo.burn_rate_estimate > 2.0 for 3m (route to runtime-oncall + infra fallback)
Also add direct 5xx rate alerts: `rate(runtime_errors_5xx[1m]) > x` per-model_family exceeding baseline.
tara: Pager routing rules I'd like to codify now:
- If alert.label.component == "kv_cache" -> pager to eng-runtime (runtime-oncall PD service)
- If alert.label.host_pool exists AND host_pool in [gpunode-*] -> pager to eng-infra (infra-oncall PD service)
- If alert severity == critical and host_pool shows OOM/eviction -> auto-escalate to infra + exec oncall
Can we attach `runbook_url` label to alerts? That helps triage.
jess: runbook_url label is fine. Also suggest a sampling rule on raw request spans: store `model_id` only for sampled traces and add `model_family` for all.
leo: Product note — dashboards should include a rollout toggle filter (feature_flag: rollout_x) so SRE/PMs can quickly compare traffic during canaries. Also want a small canary panel that shows model_family delta vs baseline.
karim: Also include `quantization_profile` label (e.g., fq8, int8) on model_family level so we can see perf changes from quant/precision toggles. Again, don't add it to every series; keep it as an optional dropdown on dashboards.
dev-bot: grafana: pushed dashboard template `runtime-telemetry-v1` to staging (id: 4302). Contains p50/p95 panels, kv cache heatmap, and SLO burn estimator panel.
maya: Summary / decisions: 1) metric names listed above accepted; 2) label schema: env, region, model_family, customer_tier (aggregates only), host_pool, shard; sample model_id at 1%; quant/profile optional dropdown; 3) alert thresholds: warning burn >1.2/10m, critical burn >2.0/3m; 4) pager routing rules as @tara described + runbook_url label; 5) grafana template pushed to staging (dev-bot) — please validate queries; 6) action items: ryan to review queries, jess to add sampling rule, anika to author alert docs + PD services mapping, tara to codify routing playbook, leo/karim to give final product/feature_flag labels.
ryan: I'll validate queries by EOD.
jess: I'll open a PR for sampling config and post the link here when ready.
anika: I'll draft the alert runbook + PD service mapping, target tomorrow morning.
tara: I'll write the pagerflow and escalation matrix, will sync with anika on labels.
leo: I'll add rollout flags to the staging dashboard and add the canary panel.
karim: I'll add quantization_profile as an optional template variable.
maya: Great — if no objections by EOD I'll merge the schema doc and we can flip on staging dashboards. Please :thumbsup: if you agree.
ryan: :thumbsup:
